Calcium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid according to the following chemical equation: $\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} + 2\text{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$
Line P on the graph shows how the volume of carbon dioxide formed changes with time when $4.0 \text{ g}$ of calcium carbonate reacts with $50 \text{ cm}^3$ of $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ hydrochloric acid at $20 \text{ °C}$.
A second reaction was carried out under identical conditions with the same mass of calcium carbonate but using $50 \text{ cm}^3$ of $2.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ hydrochloric acid.
Which line (A-F) best represents how the volume of carbon dioxide formed changes with time in the second reaction?
($M_r$ value: $\text{CaCO}_3 = 100$)
